articles.title: A Disaster for U.S. AI Supremacy
articles.content:
“An Nvidia without its Founder will be like a headless Hydra. The best possible outcome for China’s interests in the future of AI.”1
Good Morning,
The U.S. China hawks got their revenge on Jensen Huang. The downfall of Jensen Huang from Nvidia, after 33 years (He’s 63) isn’t as much a spy story as it is a National security push against China. Jensen Huang is the single person in many ways who is most the architect of the AI boom and circular financing that is now pervasive in Generative AI. He also became a close advisor and friend to the President, Donald Trump in recent quarters.
The downfall of Jensen is truly detrimental for U.S. AI Supremacy. Nvidia is one of the key benefactors of the entire GPU and large language model movement and the unrivaled focal point of the the AI buildout, a maniacal building of datacenters and a Manhattan project-esque American obsession with compute capacity since 2023. It’s also extremely unpopular with the general population. This is political.
Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it into the company that powered the AI boom, doing so with no second-in-command and extremely shaky and unusual corporate governance. By having extramarital affairs he took risks no corporate executive in the history of technology was taking. By being romantically involved with those involved in GPU smuggling he may have committed serious crimes. He may also get away with them for the most part.
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia on November 12, 2026 after the Nvidia board came to the only conclusion it could. It’s a worse moment than Sam Altman getting fired on November 17th, 2023 for both the AI industry's future and the AI bull market in stocks. In its somewhat manufactured rivalry with China, this significantly weakens the U.S.’s ability to keep in the lead in this technology.
It leaves the AI chip monopoly in a huge limbo whereby Nvidia’s board will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidate, even as investigations and congress meetings and hearings pile up. This is political theatre. Jensen Huang as a “visionary of the AI age”, was well liked, made many strategic decisions and overcame many obstacles leading Nvidia shareholders to incredible wealth. Obscene and absurd levels of wealth. He deserves our gratitude, not our mockery. Silicon Valley should stay out of Washington affairs.
It was a grave mistake for Jensen Huang, a Taiwanese-American, to enter politics. No PR firm could save him from the fallout of sleeping with what is believed to be an agent of China. Huang is a victim of the Blue Tsunami wave of the Democratic party at the Midterm elections, and there will be many more. With datacenters incredibly unpopular, Jensen Huang had become the face of the elites imposing their will on American communities, the internet and unsuspecting professions including white collar ones.
Enemies of Jensen Huang in Washington orchestrated his fall. After the China spy story, on November 11, The New York Times reported that Huang had also engaged in a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s Vice President of Healthcare, who reported directly to him. This is a no-no in Silicon Valley and especially in Nvidia’s own culture. He broke his own rules. Now about America’s own attempt to have rules that benefit itself.
U.S. export controls have not succeeded in doing anything. China has flourished in such an environment with aggressive distillation campaigns, GPU smuggling and with plentiful energy abundance and deep talent in AI researchers, China’s optics are actually fairly bright in the industry, including in robotics - sometimes called Physical AI. The U.S. cannot monopolize or control this technology. In human history the originators of a technology rarely benefit from it alone for long. Diffusion of new technologies is inevitable.
The board said it expects Nvidia’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption. But that’s impossible, this changes everything about Nvidia’s reputation and culture. Yes sure, Nvidia controls nearly 85% of the high-end data center AI GPU market by revenue and 90%+ of the discrete consumer GPU market. But suddenly and irrevocably, its best days are behind it. Jensen was more than the soul of Nvidia, he was its brain, mastermind and key-man catalyst.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was sent a highly classified memo warning about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, but failed to impose sanctions on Singapore based Megaspeed. And frankly, who knows how many other organizations like Megaspeed. Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) will continue be a legend of tech immigration stories and transformation stories in technology of how to make a crucial pivot and what led to the rise of the GPU. The most significant hardware innovation of the decade, the spark that made Generative AI LLMs possible.
The U.S. is handicapping itself with all of these probes and bizarre abuses of media manipulation for political reasons. This is so much bigger than sex, spying and smuggling. This is a takedown of historic proportions, with the aura of a witch hunt. This is the United States declawing its own leadership in AI’s most critical supply-chain. The relationship of TSMC with Nvidia. The Taiwan connection. President Trump will be meeting with President Xi, while Jensen will be testifying for lawmakers. This is poetic stupidity on so many levels.
Nvidia shares fell as much as 13% after news of Huang's resignation Thursday November 12th, after the stock is already down nearly 27% in the last month. But in the macro picture, this is a total disaster for U.S. leadership in the domain. This helps Alphabet’s entry into the TPU market as a serious player in 2027, along with rivals like AMD and gives Chinese AI chip makers a time to consolidate their efforts. China has made and is making rapid progress in both models, token share and in their own very nascent semiconductor and memory industries.
While Silicon Valley has hacked a corrupt Trump Administration, making Jensen the fall-guy is a huge mistake. With AI sentiment plummeting during 2025 and even more so in 2026, Jensen Huang will be now remembered by non-techies as a cheater. When in reality Nvidia’s rise to become the most valuable company in the world for a time is one of the biggest success stories of public markets and technological history. Only a unique leader with incredible tenacity could have achieved this. A uniquely Taiwanese work ethic. Remember that as the U.S. goes on to continue to exploit TSMC and Taiwanese companies for its own profit, corrupt self-interest and national interests.
“This is a man more important to Nvidia, than Steve jobs was to Apple.”
Export controls were never going to be effective against a technology as important as Generative AI in slowing down China. China’s open-weight models (by fair means or foul) are easily six months ahead of Western open-source models. Their AI Labs are world class. Firing (forcing him to resign due a scandal fabricated by media leaks) Jensen Huang decapitates Silicon Valley in a way that changes the future of AI. This is a man more important to Nvidia, than Steve jobs was to Apple.
I don’t personally care how many girlfriends he had, and while his relationship with Donald Trump was clearly a huge mistake, this weakens the U.S. ability to keep ahead in AI in such fundamental ways that this could have been China’s spying goal all along. Not to influence AI policy in Washington, but to discredit the Taiwan born corporate Genius. This wasn’t a sex scandal, this was a political assassination. I’ve read a lot of analysis on this story and media reports that miss the key points. The U.S. has played right into China’s hands. The lady in the pink dress, whoever she is, managed to do that. Jensen Huang’s mistake wasn’t to abuse his position in affairs of opportunism, it was to think influencing Washington was safe and justified. U.S. corporations should not have the right to lobby and become central consultants to Presidents. The alliance between Jensen Huang and Donald Trump was never going to end well.
Nvidia without Jensen Huang is easily worth 25% less, or more. It will be handicapped for months and likely will never be the same again. This is how monopolies crumble. This is infinitely more damaging than China evading Chip sanctions, sanctions that historically have been shown not to work. If anything, China’s intensity in trying to catch up in semiconductors and GPUs and memory chips and open models has never been stronger. Meanwhile the Trump Administration created toxic conditions where Jensen could be ensnared and scapegoated so easily. 33 years in engineering and entrepreneurship and founding his own company couldn't prepare him for the world of Donald Trump (and his enemies).
Jensen Huang had become a celebrity or rock-star of technology and AI culture. He was literally the face of AI for a good four years there. He was the ultimate ambassador and evangelist for U.S. American AI Supremacy. He built significant relationships and was the man at the center of the AI boom. It’s impossible for Nvidia to thrive in the same way, ever again. Since 2017, Jensen Huang’s career flourished in the next 9 years like few ever in American and human corporate history.
By losing Jensen, American loses its spark and purity in the AI race. History will show this to be a colossal mistake. Jensen Huang has been more important than Elon Musk to provide America with structural advantages in AI. This isn’t about Nvidia succession, but about an AI industry with a crisis of leadership. Jensen Huang will be bogged down in investigations and mired in family obligations and enormous stress. At 63, it’s somewhat doubtful he can rebound from this professionally in any meaningful way. Even if he returns to Nvidia one day, he won’t be the same.
Today and this week, Jensen Huang becomes a martyr. Misunderstood and twisted by China hawks and National security narratives that miss the key point. Entrepreneurs of Jensen’s calibre are generational. Sidelining him allows China to take the upper hand. Nvidia is that important. America’s attempt to hoard the technology for themselves is grossly mistaken. One nation cannot leverage a technology like Generative AI for itself, just as the internet couldn’t be controlled. It’s so ridiculous. The U.S. is destined to lose, not because it doesn’t have the biggest companies or the most aggressive compute strategy, or the most capital, but precisely because it does. And it abuses that privilege. In a mockery to the rest of the world. That’s how Empires crumble.
Jensen Huang being pushed out of Silicon Valley, is a victory for China.
Read more

articles.title: What Happens when LLMs get Smaller and On-Device?
articles.content:
With the AI market experiencing some volatility and a pull back, it’s an interesting time to analyze the narratives of the some of the biggest AI bears. Some of those I find fairly interesting are Michael Burry, Yann LeCun, David Cahn, Ed Zitron, Jim Covello, , Melanie Mitchell, Molly White, Abi Awomosu, David Rosenberg, Stacy Rasgon, Dean Baker and Gary Marcus.
But how about in Europe? Joachim Klement is an investment strategist based in London, I asked him if I could share one of his articles for a second publication. Joachim Klement is Head of Strategy, Economics, and ESG based in London working at Panmure Liberum. Throughout his professional career, Joachim focused on economics, geopolitics, ESG and their impact on financial markets.
Now I may have a soft spot for Mathematicians who predict World Cup football winners, but when the AI optimist thesis gets shaky, that’s when I think we should be reading these diverse takes on the AI bubble for the informed context and even predictions.
A lot of economists who are involved in AI write very unrealistic reports, but I myself prefer realism.
Joachim Klement’s view on small language models (SLMs) and edge device inference serves as a primary catalyst for his broader macro AI bear thesis. Rather than viewing local AI as an additive trend, he sees it as a structural threat to the economic assumptions driving centralized hyperscalers.
When I first read his summary and position, I found it so persuasive I contacted him immediately. I will add that the DeepSeek moment, never really went away. And I think Claude Mythos 5.2 will do great. I just believe how the world uses these models is also going to change.
“My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement said in an interview.
October 9th, 2026 segment (video) with Bloomberg, that summarizes our thesis today.
Jensen Huang affair not on my Bingo Card (CNBC).
China is decoupling from the West
Europeans really don’t like to invest in stocks
It’s not you, it’s your AI
As the Generative AI cycle matures it won’t just be more capable models, agents and open-source counterpoint guiding consumption patterns.
🔸 The Death of the "Bigger is Better" Paradigm
🔸 Upfront Capex vs. Edge Efficiency
🔸Margin Compression and Unprofitability
🔸Hardware Pivot as a Hedge
In Klement's view, the future of AI technology will be small, efficient, and cheap—making the business model powering centralized cloud AI structurally unprofitable.
In recent interviews Klement has stated he could see the S&P 500 falling to around 5,000 by end-2027. Currently it rests at about 7,500. That’s only a 33% drop. Historically the S&P goes up 7-10% a year, but since 2020 it’s been up 16.4%. That’s not normal. Mean reversion is its own kind of realism, whatever the external catalysts (or theories or narratives) may be.
The model is significantly better and faster. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also comes with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. They already generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors. The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released a “frontier” model since AI Execs like Dario Amodei were calling for a slowdown. Anthropic will have to IPO significantly lower than previously anticipated.
“We called for pacing, not pausing,” Dianne Penn, Anthropic’s head of product management
Anthropic is clearly the frontier model builder and AI Lab of its generation. Though I wouldn’t count the likes of DeepSeek out quite yet. The most stand-out feature of Mythos 5.2 is how it redefines autonomous engineering thus allowing Anthropic’s cadence of new model releases to be noticeably faster. The model now is better equipped and admits when it doesn't know things instead of hallucinating.
It’s been almost three months since this article was first published, but in view of the almost bear market on Semis, Neo Clouds and pressure on the AI sector, I think it deserves fresh eyeballs.
Read the following very carefully. If you were an executive at Apple, you might have paid special attention to this point of view and indeed in 2023 itself. If you value his unique takes, please support the author and signal your appreciation for the analysis.
By
In my regular research (behind a paywall), I have been saying for a while that I think the future of AI is not large language models (LLM), but small language models (SLM) run on local desktop computers or even mobile phones. In May, a team from Stanford University published research that compared these SLMs with the performance of LLMs run in data centres. If their results are true, then we will hardly need any data centres in the future, and the hyperscalers are wasting hundreds of billions of dollars in investments.
Seriously, if you are an investor trying to figure out where to invest in the AI hype, you need to read this paper in full. But to get you started, let me give you some highlights.
First, they ran a series of SLMs (QWEN 3, GEMMA 3, GPT-OSS, GRANITE 4.0) that can be downloaded on a local PC and compared their performance with cloud-based state-of-the-art LLMs (ChatGPT 5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro).
They ran these SLMs on local PCs powered either by an Nvidia chip or an Apple M4 chip, as they are readily available in current high-end desktop computers (the entire study was done before Nvidia presented its AI chip for PCs, which will only accelerate the move away from datacentres to models run on desktops).
Then they traced the performance of these SLMs vs LLM between 2023 and October 2025 on both chat tasks and reasoning tasks.
The chart below shows the Win/Tie-ratio for SLMs vs LLMs in chat requests, which still make up the vast majority of requests today. As you can see, in every domain, the best SLM is able to find the same or better answers than an LLM in 90% or more of the cases, with an average across all domains of 98.6%.
Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in chat requests
When it comes to reasoning tasks, which are obviously more demanding, SLMs are catching up fast. On average, they provide a better or at least as good an answer as LLMs in 62.5% of the cases.
Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in reasoning tasks
However, in real life, the tasks for SLMs and LLMs are typically a mix of chat requests and reasoning tasks, so the third chart shows the weighted average of chat request performance and reasoning performance based on the frequency of tasks in each domain. As you can see, on average, SLMs are as good if not better than LLMs in 81.2% of the cases, with the LLMs having a significant advantage only in areas like engineering, life sciences, transportation and computer sciences.
Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in chat and reasoning tasks
But it’s not just accuracy. SLMs achieve this performance at energy and compute costs that are between 50% and 85% lower than for an LLM, depending on the SLM and hardware used in the computer.
What is more, SLMs are catching up rapidly in reasoning tasks. The final chart shows the performance of SLMs as a function of difficulty level and model generation for reasoning tasks alone.
In 2023, the success rate of SLMs in reasoning tasks was typically 50% or so across all five difficulty levels. By October 2025, the SLMs achieved 99% success for the easiest reasoning tasks in levels 1 and 2, 85% to 92% success in harder tasks (levels 3 and 4) and only lagged LLMs in the hardest tasks of level 5 (51.5% success rate).
Success rates of SLMs in reasoning tasks
This already means that one can replace data centres and their expensive cutting-edge semiconductor infrastructure in four out of five use cases. The research report estimates that the addressable market in the US for SLMs has grown to about $10tn or one-third of the entire US GDP of $30tn. There isn’t much left for LLMs to thrive in, and every year, their advantage over SLMs is shrinking.
There clearly are areas where LLMs are still way ahead, particularly in agentic AI applications, where SLMs currently only achieve accuracy and success rates of less than 50%. Similarly, it is difficult to run these SLMs on smartphones so far. The models that can be run on an iPhone are significantly worse than the models that can be run on a desktop PC.
But – and this is important – the models run on a desktop PC, and even more so, the ones run on a smartphone are much more energy efficient than the ones run in the cloud. The inference per Watt of these SLMs is typically seven times larger than that of LLMs. And that means that when you encounter a task that can be solved on a desktop or even a mobile device, it is cheaper to do so locally than send it to a data centre.
This has important implications for investors, in my view:
We need many fewer data centres than we think. If we can already replace 70% to 80% of the tasks that are expected to run on LLMs with SLMs, the hyperscalers have simply no revenue growth in the future that is nearly enough to justify the capex. In fact, if this research is true and this trend continues, data centres may be the worst investment in the AI space one can make right now.
While we continue to need enormous investments in semiconductors of all sorts, we do not need to invest in the most advanced Nvidia chips. The cheaper ones that run on desktop PCs will be enough. The best case for Nvidia is that it can replace its high-end data centre GPUs with its new chips for desktop PCs. What will that do to Nvidia’s margins and revenue growth going forward?
We still need LLMs for the most advanced tasks, and companies like OpenAI, Anthropic and others will be able to ‘dumb down’ their models to an SLM and sell them instead of LLMs. But given the already fierce competition from Chinese providers like QWEN or IBM’s GRANITE, the profit margins for these models will be much smaller than for LLMs. So what does that mean for the valuation of these companies in their planned IPOs and their growth trajectory?
While agentic AI is still better on LLMs, this may only be a temporary advantage, similar to what we have seen in reasoning tasks and single chat requests. If that is the case, the true winners of the AI boom will not be the providers of advanced hardware and data centres but the boring manufacturers of desktop computers like Dell and Apple.
Watching this race unfold is going to be fun, and I am increasingly convinced that many people will be badly burned because they invest in the wrong technology.

With the AI market experiencing some volatility and a pull back, it’s an interesting time to analyze the narratives of the some of the biggest AI bears. Some of those I find fairly interesting are Michael Burry, Yann LeCun, David Cahn, Ed Zitron, Jim Covello, , Melanie Mitchell, Molly White, Abi Awomosu, David Rosenberg, Stacy Rasgon, Dean Baker and Gary Marcus.

What do European Voices have to do with the American AI Bull Market?

But how about in Europe? Joachim Klement is an investment strategist based in London, I asked him if I could share one of his articles for a second publication. Joachim Klement is Head of Strategy, Economics, and ESG based in London working at Panmure Liberum. Throughout his professional career, Joachim focused on economics, geopolitics, ESG and their impact on financial markets.

Now I may have a soft spot for Mathematicians who predict World Cup football winners, but when the AI optimist thesis gets shaky, that’s when I think we should be reading these diverse takes on the AI bubble for the informed context and even predictions.

Klement on Investing

Klement on Investing
Thoughts on financial markets by a grumpy, middle-aged German. What more do you want?
By Joachim Klement

A lot of economists who are involved in AI write very unrealistic reports, but I myself prefer realism.

Thesis on SLMs

Joachim Klement’s view on small language models (SLMs) and edge device inference serves as a primary catalyst for his broader macro AI bear thesis. Rather than viewing local AI as an additive trend, he sees it as a structural threat to the economic assumptions driving centralized hyperscalers.

When I first read his summary and position, I found it so persuasive I contacted him immediately. I will add that the DeepSeek moment, never really went away. And I think Claude Mythos 5.2 will do great. I just believe how the world uses these models is also going to change.

View the latest Flagship Model

“My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement said in an interview.

Selection of Klement

  • October 9th, 2026 segment (video) with Bloomberg, that summarizes our thesis today.

  • Jensen Huang affair not on my Bingo Card (CNBC).

  • China is decoupling from the West

  • Europeans really don’t like to invest in stocks

  • It’s not you, it’s your AI

Themes and Highlights

As the Generative AI cycle matures it won’t just be more capable models, agents and open-source counterpoint guiding consumption patterns.

🔸 The Death of the "Bigger is Better" Paradigm

🔸 Upfront Capex vs. Edge Efficiency

🔸Margin Compression and Unprofitability

🔸Hardware Pivot as a Hedge

In Klement's view, the future of AI technology will be small, efficient, and cheap—making the business model powering centralized cloud AI structurally unprofitable.

In recent interviews Klement has stated he could see the S&P 500 falling to around 5,000 by end-2027. Currently it rests at about 7,500. That’s only a 33% drop. Historically the S&P goes up 7-10% a year, but since 2020 it’s been up 16.4%. That’s not normal. Mean reversion is its own kind of realism, whatever the external catalysts (or theories or narratives) may be.

Mythos / Fable 5.2 is a Superb Model

The model is significantly better and faster. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also comes with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. They already generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors. The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released a “frontier” model since AI Execs like Dario Amodei were calling for a slowdown. Anthropic will have to IPO significantly lower than previously anticipated.

“We called for pacing, not pausing,” Dianne Penn, Anthropic’s head of product management

Anthropic is clearly the frontier model builder and AI Lab of its generation. Though I wouldn’t count the likes of DeepSeek out quite yet. The most stand-out feature of Mythos 5.2 is how it redefines autonomous engineering thus allowing Anthropic’s cadence of new model releases to be noticeably faster. The model now is better equipped and admits when it doesn't know things instead of hallucinating.

It’s been almost three months since this article was first published, but in view of the almost bear market on Semis, Neo Clouds and pressure on the AI sector, I think it deserves fresh eyeballs.

Read the following very carefully. If you were an executive at Apple, you might have paid special attention to this point of view and indeed in 2023 itself. If you value his unique takes, please support the author and signal your appreciation for the analysis.

Pledge your Support to Klement

If this is true, the hyperscalers are toast

By

In my regular research (behind a paywall), I have been saying for a while that I think the future of AI is not large language models (LLM), but small language models (SLM) run on local desktop computers or even mobile phones. In May, a team from Stanford University published research that compared these SLMs with the performance of LLMs run in data centres. If their results are true, then we will hardly need any data centres in the future, and the hyperscalers are wasting hundreds of billions of dollars in investments.

Seriously, if you are an investor trying to figure out where to invest in the AI hype, you need to read this paper in full. But to get you started, let me give you some highlights.

First, they ran a series of SLMs (QWEN 3, GEMMA 3, GPT-OSS, GRANITE 4.0) that can be downloaded on a local PC and compared their performance with cloud-based state-of-the-art LLMs (ChatGPT 5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro).

They ran these SLMs on local PCs powered either by an Nvidia chip or an Apple M4 chip, as they are readily available in current high-end desktop computers (the entire study was done before Nvidia presented its AI chip for PCs, which will only accelerate the move away from datacentres to models run on desktops).

Then they traced the performance of these SLMs vs LLM between 2023 and October 2025 on both chat tasks and reasoning tasks.

The chart below shows the Win/Tie-ratio for SLMs vs LLMs in chat requests, which still make up the vast majority of requests today. As you can see, in every domain, the best SLM is able to find the same or better answers than an LLM in 90% or more of the cases, with an average across all domains of 98.6%.

Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in chat requests

When it comes to reasoning tasks, which are obviously more demanding, SLMs are catching up fast. On average, they provide a better or at least as good an answer as LLMs in 62.5% of the cases.

Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in reasoning tasks

However, in real life, the tasks for SLMs and LLMs are typically a mix of chat requests and reasoning tasks, so the third chart shows the weighted average of chat request performance and reasoning performance based on the frequency of tasks in each domain. As you can see, on average, SLMs are as good if not better than LLMs in 81.2% of the cases, with the LLMs having a significant advantage only in areas like engineering, life sciences, transportation and computer sciences.

Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in chat and reasoning tasks

But it’s not just accuracy. SLMs achieve this performance at energy and compute costs that are between 50% and 85% lower than for an LLM, depending on the SLM and hardware used in the computer.

What is more, SLMs are catching up rapidly in reasoning tasks. The final chart shows the performance of SLMs as a function of difficulty level and model generation for reasoning tasks alone.

In 2023, the success rate of SLMs in reasoning tasks was typically 50% or so across all five difficulty levels. By October 2025, the SLMs achieved 99% success for the easiest reasoning tasks in levels 1 and 2, 85% to 92% success in harder tasks (levels 3 and 4) and only lagged LLMs in the hardest tasks of level 5 (51.5% success rate).

Success rates of SLMs in reasoning tasks

This already means that one can replace data centres and their expensive cutting-edge semiconductor infrastructure in four out of five use cases. The research report estimates that the addressable market in the US for SLMs has grown to about $10tn or one-third of the entire US GDP of $30tn. There isn’t much left for LLMs to thrive in, and every year, their advantage over SLMs is shrinking.

There clearly are areas where LLMs are still way ahead, particularly in agentic AI applications, where SLMs currently only achieve accuracy and success rates of less than 50%. Similarly, it is difficult to run these SLMs on smartphones so far. The models that can be run on an iPhone are significantly worse than the models that can be run on a desktop PC.

But – and this is important – the models run on a desktop PC, and even more so, the ones run on a smartphone are much more energy efficient than the ones run in the cloud. The inference per Watt of these SLMs is typically seven times larger than that of LLMs. And that means that when you encounter a task that can be solved on a desktop or even a mobile device, it is cheaper to do so locally than send it to a data centre.

This has important implications for investors, in my view:

  • We need many fewer data centres than we think. If we can already replace 70% to 80% of the tasks that are expected to run on LLMs with SLMs, the hyperscalers have simply no revenue growth in the future that is nearly enough to justify the capex. In fact, if this research is true and this trend continues, data centres may be the worst investment in the AI space one can make right now.

  • While we continue to need enormous investments in semiconductors of all sorts, we do not need to invest in the most advanced Nvidia chips. The cheaper ones that run on desktop PCs will be enough.   • While agentic AI is still better on LLMs, this may only be a temporary advantage, similar to what we have seen in reasoning tasks and single chat requests. If that is the case, the true winners of the AI boom will not be the providers of advanced hardware and data centres but the boring manufacturers of desktop computers like Dell and Apple.

Watching this race unfold is going to be fun, and I am increasingly convinced that many people will be badly burned because they invest in the wrong technology.

articles.title: AI is a Honeypot Story 🍯🧸
articles.content:
Dear Readers,
Every now and again the AI trade gets real. At the exact moment when Jensen Huang of Nvidia was most influential with Donald Trump (back mid 2025 to early 2026), there was something else going on in his personal life. This weekend it came out that the Nvidia CEO sent staff in an email that he had an affair and that the company’s board has opened an independent investigation into allegations that the woman is a Chinese spy. This is the transcript of the Email:
Subject: A message to our company
Body: “I owe my family and all of you an apology.
I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.
Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.
To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.
To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me.
Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.
Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company, and I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.
My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.” - Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO.
Jensen Huang's most significant involvement with Alice Huang (also known as Huang Le), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, spans from mid-2024 through early 2026. This was the most critical period when China managed to obtain access to many of Nvidia’s critical GPUs and AI chips and who essentially caught up in the open-source AI race. Nvidia's board said an independent committee, assisted by outside counsel, will investigate the matter.
During the same period of the affair, Jensen Huang struck up a very close rapport with the POTUS and the spy’s (overreach) mission may have already been completed at this time. Huang has been a key voice in Washington pushing to loosen restrictions on AI chip sales to China.
While the AI trade tetters on the bring of a bear market, Nvidia’s stock was down 4% after the story broke. Despite strict U.S. export controls aimed at restricting China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence hardware (such as Nvidia's A100, H100, B200, and B300 chips). These tactics include shell companies in places like Singapore, Malaysia, the UAE and Hong Kong, among others. Chinese organizations have created a variety of mechanisms including overseas subsidiaries or shell entities in intermediary countries to lease server space equipped with top-tier Nvidia clusters.
Jensen Huang has long argued that keeping American technology in the Chinese market strengthens U.S. competitiveness and prevented China from developing their own potentially more advanced chips. Now in late 2026, we don’t know how much influence Alice Huang had on his viewpoints and opinions. His talking points could have come from in part, the highest levels of China. (I actually agree with him that the restrictions have actually helped China innovate in the sector and have been counter-productive). Jensen Huang has impacted AI policy more than any other Tech executive in the world, so that’s why this is a big deal.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned top Trump officials about Huang's relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believed was a Chinese spy, The New York Times (NYT) reported Friday. In the days following, there’s been a ramp up of pressure. The Midterm “Blue Tsunami” wave and now Jensen’s spy story truly is bearish for the AI bull market. Donald Trump knew about the situation for at least a year and didn’t want it to hamper AI chip sales. The plot is like a honeypot spy movie plot, but has real ramifications for AI history and U.S. National security.
Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.) promised a probe of the latest Times report and Huang’s relationships.
He went on to say via Axios, “The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I’m convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn’t corrupt. Congress will investigate and get answers,” Coons posted to X, linking in another post to the Times’ story.
From what we can tell from the investigative journalism by U.S. outlets, the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to seek information and potentially push for Nvidia’s advanced chips to be made available in China, countering existing restrictions, the Times reported. It appears the affair led to a successful mission for China at a considerable cost to the Nvidia’s CEO personal life.
With so much concentration of power in the U.S’s approach to AI supremacy, honeypot spy stories of this nature become increasingly dangerous. Jensen Huang has long argued that restricting Nvidia's access to China risks undermining America's technological advantage and while his affairs don’t change the merits of his viewpoint, his proximity to Trump during that period is a serious cause for concern - there would be a lot that we still don’t know.
President Donald Trump backed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Sunday:
"I think he's an honorable guy," Trump told reporters on Sunday. "I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it."
A bear market and a spy story, this is America.
At 6:00 PM ET, US stock market futures opened for the first time since Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a "relationship" with a Chinese spy.

articles.title: Is Recursive Self-Improvement the Moat of Anthropic?
articles.content:
Good Morning,
I have been absorbing the stunning Midterm “blue wave” elections results and what it means for datacenter moratoriums and a BigTech backlash. While Anthropic this week revealed its amended or revised S-1/A with its particularly weird warnings around about being near to RSI is its best attempt at a marketing pitch or an IPO stunt. Anthropic, an AI startup whose ties to Amazon and Alphabet are so solid you could consider circular financing itself to be its real moat and competitive advantage that is ANT’s distinct and unusual position of privilege.
The concentration of premium token spend of the top Enterprise AI customers is certainly also about a result of having consistently the top frontier models, that is perhaps the result of having recruited the highest paid AI researcher and being able to retain them1. All this is quite stunning for a company that’s just five years old. Recently Menlo (who is an early investor in Anthropic), release their latest State of Enterprise AI report.
Anthropic (not Palantir) has been the key beneficiary of Enterprise AI concentration being the moat of the Generative AI movement. While AI adoption is not as great as some AI optimists would have you believe, Enterprise AI is scaling in the 2020s. Anthropic is at the frontier of that ramp and it certainly looks like a winner-takes-all leadership. We found out in 2026 that Google or OpenAI are struggling to keep up.
Enterprise generative AI deployment spending is a thing in process that has grown roughly 100x in three years. It went from $1.7B in 2023 to $8.5B in 2024 (5.0x) and $33B in 2025 (3.9x). By September 2026, spending reached $176.8B, up 5.4x from last year. Anthropic owns the top end of all of this due to its dominant AI coding models that are also proficient in Agentic AI.
This has very little to do with speculative recursive self-improvement (RSI) capabilities, or Claude being able to help train its next generation of frontier models (faster), and everything to do with the capital Anthropic has been able to raise where Alphabet and Amazon have significant equity stakes in the business, accompanied by Cloud partnerships and a diversified financial backing across Technology.
Anthropic’s RSI marketing stunt reeks of the desperation of an overvalued IPO. Of Billionaire co-founders pretending, they are ambassadors of the new world. As growth slows this will be an important marketing angle to monitor.
America and their duopolies. BigAI is following a familiar patterns with Anthropic and OpenAI. American seems a capitalism of dualities, with industries typically having just two major winners.
Anthropic’s S-1 and the wishful oratory of its CEO keeps on a marketing hacks that is both a boast and a warning that the company is on the cusp of creating a model capable of recursive self-improvement (RSI). But true RSI would be general and across industries and totally autonomous, not some gimmick of Claude Code building the next Claude Opus model or accelerating the cadence a bit faster. In a world where AI is not leading much in the real economy, Anthropic’s exhibition of RSI needs some fact checking. Generative AI is conspicuously absent from being meaningful contributor to productivity in the real world.
Anthropic’s concentration of the top AI researchers and its ability to retain them has been pretty uncanny since 2023 which has contributed to a significant edge. Whereby its LLMs are significantly ahead of OpenAI and Google, it’s closest American rivals. If talent, access to capital and BigTech’s hyperscaler support isn’t a moat, I don’t know what is. In these days of watered down AGI and RSI definitions, that are mere shadows of their original definitions, RSI is the point at which AI grows so good at training itself that it spawns a dramatic acceleration of AI capabilities. Meanwhile agent swarms feel more like cybersecurity threats and layoff pressures in 2026, rather than significant new capabilities for most of us in society and in the labor market.
Anthropic's own language around RSI is itself disturbing, grandiose and feels fundamentally out of touch. Anthropic’s models are valuable mostly for their AI coding supremacy and Claude Code’s share of the top spectrum of Spend at the biggest American companies may only be temporary. There’s no guarantee Anthropic is the last answer to this equation.
The Midterms significantly extends Moratoriums and delays many datacenters stuck in limbo due to various bottlenecks. The “Blue Tsunami” could also results in Elon Musk, Starlink and other investigations and public hearings by Congress with increasing regulatory scrutiny. Billionaires were on the ballot and the Republic has spoken.
James Talarico’s victory in the US Senate race and Gina Hinojosa’s defeat of three-term Governor Greg Abbott in the State of Texas stole the headlines, symbolic because it has become the datacenter capital of AI where Billionaires have moved, which is the ultimate irony. Talarico made AI datacenters a central argument of his campaign.
Roughly a quarter of the US data center capacity expected to come online by 2030 is in Texas, and Jefferies estimates that some 13.3 gigawatts of announced projects would be at risk under a Hinojosa moratorium.
Georgia and Ohio, two other large pipeline states, also elected Democratic governors who have promised a pause or a conditional freeze2.
Texas, Georgia, Ohio.
